DUMMY/2136.wav|dynamic reauthorization. the traditional authorization scheme in which the system checks the amount of available funds at the end of a call has many drawbacks. for one, the system does not react to balance changes, refunds, payments, or charges made while the call is in progress. there is also the possibility of overdrafts in the case of multiple simultaneous calls are allowed, and so on. this is why portabilling now offers you the ability to reauthorize the user's activity dynamically. while a session, for example voice call, is in progress, the system reserves a small portion of the available funds to cover the next short time interval, for example one minute. as the end of this interval comes near, the system attempts to reserve funds to cover the next interval and so on. if no remaining funds are available, the call is disconnected. so if a customer sends an sms message during a phone call, decreasing the available funds, or makes a credit card payment, increasing the available funds. this immediately affects the call, whether it will be disconnected sooner or the maximum allowed call time will increase.

DUMMY/2202.wav|call keep alive monitoring a typical problem in a voip scenario is that if your customer loses internet connectivity while a call is in progress, no further information is received from the ip phone. unless this is detected promptly and the other segment of the call is disconnected, it may lead to hung calls with a very long duration, incorrect charges, and billing disputes. to prevent this, portisip includes a special keep alive module. for every call which is still in progress, portasip periodically sends sip messages to both the caller and the called party. if one party does not reply to the message, even after several retransmits, it is clear that it has gone offline and so the call is immediately disconnected. portasip's keep alive feature allows call processing problems to be avoided when a customer loses internet connectivity.

DUMMY/2209.wav|portasip performance a single portasip server can process up to fifty thousand concurrent registrations and fifty call attempts per second. what exactly does this mean? it means that fifty thousand IP phones can be online on your network at the same time and that up to fifty users can start a new phone call every second. how many simultaneous or concurrent calls does that translate into? it mainly depends on the average call duration and call success rate. assuming the industry norms of an average call duration of five minutes and a call success rate of fifty percent, this adds up to seven thousand five hundred concurrent calls. this means that seven thousand five hundred of your customers can be talking on the phone at the same time. this scenario assumes that portasip is only handling signaling communications and that the media stream goes directly between endpoints. if portasip were to handle the media proxying as well. this would require the processing of a significant amount of network traffic. therefore, each server should be handling about two thousand concurrent calls to ensure that voice quality will not degrade due to packet delays. if you plan to have more subscribers or more simultaneous phone calls than this, you can scale up your network performance by adding another portasip server. this will increase not only your total network capacity but also your service reliability since the portasip servers will be working as a cluster. portasip is capable of processing fifty call initiations per second which translates into approximately seven thousand five hundred concurrent calls. for increased performance you can use multiple portasip servers combined into a cluster.

DUMMY/4541.wav|porta billing performance porta billing can process more than three hundred radius requests per second. now, what exactly does that mean? every call attempt or completed call on your network generates several radius requests, while the total number and type of these requests depend on the type of service being provided. for ip-centric services, which involve call routing, it translates to about fifty call initiations per second. second, while for post-paid services, the number is about seventy five call initiations per second. so a conservative estimate for port-a-billing processing speed is fifty session initiations per second. this means that up to fifty users can start a new phone call on your network every second. how many simultaneous concurrent calls does that translate to? this primarily depends on the average call duration and call success rate. assuming an average call duration of five minutes and a call success rate of fifty percent, the industry norms. this will yield more than seven thousand five hundred concurrent calls. so seven thousand five hundred of your customers can be talking on the phone at the same time. how many minutes of monthly traffic can porta billings support? again, this mainly depends on your traffic patterns, the ratio between your peak and off-peak hours, and call success rate. based on typical traffic patterns with daily peak hours, medium load hours, and off-peak hours, fifty call attempts per second will generate more than twenty million minutes per month. in order to scale up performance or provide uninterrupted service, even if there is a hardware failure on a server, it is possible to join several portabilling servers in a billing cluster. this distributes the processing of requests among all the servers and so if one of the servers in the cluster goes down, the remaining servers redistribute the load. thus, the services on your network are not interrupted. the total performance capacity grows linearly when you add more servers to the cluster. for example, a cluster of three billing nodes can process up to one hundred and fifty call attempts per second. a single port-a-billing server is capable of processing fifty to seventy five call initiations per second. this translates into approximately seven thousand five hundred concurrent calls or more than twenty million call minutes per month. installing additional porta billing servers and forming a billing cluster provides full reliability in case of hardware failure and increases the total processing capacity.

"'and we've produced all the things that go to make civilization. oh, science and art and all that, do you see?' there was something pathetic in his concentration— as if his complacency, more acute than of old, was not enough to him anymore. when, almost immediately, the telephone rang inside and the butler left the porch, daisy seized the momentary interruption and leaned toward me. i'll tell you a family secret, she whispered enthusiastically. it's about the butler's nose. do you want to hear about the butler's nose? that's why i came over tonight. well, he wasn't always a butler. he used to be the silver polisher for some people in new york that had a silver service for two hundred people. he had to polish it from morning till night, until it finally began to affect his nose. things went from bad to worse, suggested miss baker. yes, things went from bad to worse, until finally he had to give up his position. for a moment the last sunshine fell with romantic affection upon her glowing face. her voice compelled me forward breathlessly as i listened. then the glow faded, each light deserting her with lingering regret, like children leaving a pleasant street at dusk. the butler came back and murmured something close to tom's ear, whereupon tom frowned, pushed back his chair, and without a word went inside. as if his absence quickened something within her, daisy leaned forward again, her voice glowing and singing. "'i'd love to see you at my table, nick. you remind me of a—of a rose, an absolute rose.' doesn't he? he turned to miss baker for confirmation. an absolute rose! this was untrue. i am not even faintly like a rose. she was only extemporizing. but a stirring warmth flowed from her, as if her heart was trying to come out to you. concealed in one of those breathless, thrilling words. then suddenly, she threw her napkin on the table and excused herself and went into the house. miss baker and i exchanged a short glance, consciously, devoid of meaning. i was about to speak when she sat up alertly and said, "'shh!' in a warning voice. a subdued, impassioned murmur was audible in the room beyond, and miss baker leaned forward, unashamed, trying to hear. the murmur trembled on the verge of coherence, sank down, mounted excitedly, and then ceased altogether. "'this mr. gatsby you spoke of is my neighbor,' i said. "'don't talk. i want to hear what happens.' is something happening? i inquired innocently. you mean to say you don't know, said miss baker, honestly surprised. i thought everybody knew. i don't. why, she said hesitantly, tom's got some woman in new york. got some woman, i repeated blankly. miss baker nodded. she might have the decency not to telephone him at dinner time, don't you think? almost before i grasped her meaning, there was the flutter of a dress and the crunch of leather boots. and tom and daisy were back at the table.
